# Design notes

<!-- Generated by `rake docs:index` from each note's summary block; edit the notes (and spec/docs_index.rb's GROUPS), not this file. -->

One note per subsystem: the design decisions with their dates, measurements, research, and where things render.  Read the topic's note before changing a subsystem, and update the note (its summary block too, then `rake docs:index`) when its behavior changes.

## Signal graph

### [Core Abstraction: GraphNode DSL](graph_nodes.md)

`GraphNode` (`lib/mb/sound/graph_node.rb`) is mixed into any class with `#sample` and gives the fluent DSL (`123.hz.saw.lp4(800).softclip`); DSL methods live in `lib/mb/sound/graph_node/*_methods.rb`, node types in `lib/mb/sound/graph_node/`, traversal in `Traversable`.  Every consumer calls `get_sampler` on the nodes it stores, so shared nodes branch through a `Tee` (lockstep branches share one frozen buffer: copy a buffer before modifying it only if `buf.frozen?`).  Sums ring until every input ends (`.ring(:first)` opts out), products end with their first input; `node.at(x)` scales any node; DSL names are reserved on node classes.

### [Graph I/O (recipes and Ruby export)](graph_io.md)

Every graph remembers the DSL calls that built it (`GraphNode::Recipe`, `lib/mb/sound/graph_node/recipe.rb`), so `node.to_ruby` prints it back as Ruby, and graph documents (`.mbg.rb`, `lib/mb/sound/graph_io.rb` + `graph_io/`: `save`, `preset`, `GraphIO.load`/`.dump`) save graphs, clips, bundles with assets, racks, and whole sets.  Documents load by walking the Prism tree through `GraphIO::Registry`, never eval; file reads go through `GraphIO::FileGuard`.  A new DSL method taking a build block goes in `BUILD_BLOCKS`; one that reads files or allocates by an argument goes in `Registry::FILE_METHODS` or `Loader#check_limits`.

### [The library: entries, index, shelves, heads](library.md)

Every named thing (presets at every scale: effects, instruments, kits, clips, masters, sets) is a frozen `Library::Entry` in one `Library.index` (`lib/mb/sound/library.rb` + `library/`), found by name, by `find 'dark bass'`, or through the `L.fx`/`L.inst`/`L.kit` heads.  Classes with presets `extend Presettable` (one `preset` line each); shelves are searched session racks, project, user (a git repository), gems, then built-ins, and the first match wins.  `save` never replaces (`save!`, `bump: true`); library files load through `Library::FileLoader`, never eval; tracks take instrument entries as patches.  `Library::Bench` (`L.fx.reverb.bench`, `bin/preset_bench.rb reverb`) renders presets on standard material, loudness-matched, as Listening Bench sets (`--vs` before/after, `--notes` reads verdicts back); `entry.audition(:break)` is one of those graphs.

### [Plan layer (fused regions)](plan_layer.md)

`lib/mb/sound/plan.rb` + `plan/` (executor `ext/mb/sound/fast_plan`) runs connected regions of a graph as one op list per block in C, installed automatically by `Synth` and `Session#add`: an as-if transformation (the same samples bit for bit, the user's graph untouched, node state kept in the nodes), with lane groups across same-shape regions and rebuilds off the render thread.  Nodes join through `Plan::Describable` (`plan_describe`, `plan_inputs`, snapshots); call `Plan.changed(node)` after structural edits, and `Plan.explain(graph)` says why nodes stay unfused.  `MB_SOUND_PLAN=0|ruby`, `MB_SOUND_PLAN_CHECK=1`; specs use `plan_compare`, `rake plan:changed` decides on the 21-size sweep.

### [Feedback loops](feedback_loops.md)

`sig.feedback { |fb, input| input + fb.delay(5.ms) * 0.8 }` (alias `fb`; `GraphNode::FeedbackLoop`) runs a loop's nodes one sample at a time as plan ops in C (`fast_loop`, exact Ruby mirror), the same output at any block size; `sig.delay(t, feedback: g) { |d| d.fb { ... }; d.wet { ... } }` is the tape-echo insert form.  Loop ops: arithmetic, shapers, delays, SVFs, biquads, lp4/diode ladders; other nodes on the loop go through `MB::Sound.live_error`.  Latency compensation (`compensate:` `:pitch` default, `:echo`, `:dc`, `false`) keeps periods and echo times exact; a hidden high shelf sustains loops with gentle lowpasses.

### [C Extensions (compiled via rake-compiler)](c_extensions.md)

25 C extensions under `ext/mb/sound/` (plus `ext/mb/fast_sound/` and mb-term's `fast_term`), each building `lib/mb/sound/<name>.so` (`rake compile`).  New C code goes in purpose-specific extensions, not `fast_sound`; shared helpers are `static inline` in `ext/mb/sound/include/mb_ext_helpers.h` and shared kernels in `ext/mb/sound/include/mb_*.h`.  Every kernel has a Ruby reference that specs compare with it (existing ones exact mirrors, several built with `-ffp-contract=off`; new ones may use a stated tolerance).  `depend` files list each extension's headers (`rake depend:check`); a change to ext/ structure refreshes the memcheck map.

### [Sound guards: the golden set and perceptual fingerprints](sound_guards.md)

"Ears win": sound is the test, exactness only where it is heard or a workflow needs it.  The golden set (`golden/set.rb`: song scripts and presets across the maintainer's genres) is re-rendered by `rake golden:check` and compared by perceptual fingerprints (`MB::Sound::SoundGuard`, `lib/mb/sound/sound_guard/`) against calibrated thresholds.  Changes to DSP, presets, or the plan layer run it; a failure goes to the maintainer as a Bench set and only his verdict re-approves (`rake golden:approve[name] RUN=dir`), never an agent.

## Values, time, and channels

### [Numeric Mixins](numbers_lengths_phases.md)

`lib/mb/sound/numeric_sound_mixins.rb` adds `.hz`, `.db`, `.meters`, `.bits` to Numeric: `440.hz` is a `Pitch` (a sine when used as a signal; `Note < Pitch` follows the session `Tuning`), `-6.db` a `Decibels` (the linear gain that remembers its dB).  One rule for dB-valued arguments: Decibels read exactly, bare numbers are linear gains, bare negatives raise (live mode: dB with a warning).  Phases are in cycles everywhere (`MB::Sound::Phase`); lengths (`2.bars`, `250.ms`, `5.samples`) work wherever lengths do, plain numbers in each method's usual unit; `Interval`s and `Scale`s for pitch steps.

### [Params: one declaration record (`MB::Sound::Param`)](params.md)

`MB::Sound::Param` (`lib/mb/sound/param.rb`) is the one frozen declaration record: knob specs, MIDI control specs, script options, graph-document `param`/`knob` lines, rack knobs, ChannelMixer params, and ArgTypes signatures all build one.  Types and units come from the values (`2400.hz`, `-12.db`), names imply ranges, `(lo..hi).at(default)` is the canonical ranged default, Integer ranges are steps; `#position`/`#value` map along range and curve.  Checks run at declaration, load, build, and turn (never per sample), through `live_error`; a guard spec checks every declaration in lib/, presets/, and bin/.

### [Type-dispatched parameters (`MB::Sound::ArgTypes`)](arg_types.md)

`MB::Sound::ArgTypes` (`lib/mb/sound/arg_types.rb`) classifies argument values by type (tempo, ratio, seconds, samples, frequency including tagged `v.freq`, name, ...) from one ordered table, matches them against Signatures (keyword > type > position; canonical forms print keywords), and dispatches one method name to meanings by type through per-receiver Dispatch tables (`clip.clocked(x)`, `clip.at(x)`, `clip.over(x)`).  Errors and `help :at`/`:over` pages come from the tables, and a guard spec covers every row; the toolkit methods will adopt it ("Adopting it in a method" below).

### [Tweening curves](curves.md)

`MB::Sound::Curve` (`Curve[:elastic, overshoot:]`, many named easings with `_in`/`_out` variants, `Curve.db`/`Curve.s`, `bezier`, Procs; `#lookup` tables in C) maps progress 0..1 and is shared by glides (`v.hz.glide(t, shape:)`), tweens (`tween([300.hz, 3000.hz], 1.bar, curve:)`: the length is per step between keyframes, not the total), `smooth(t, curve:)`, and the antialiased shaper `sig.ease(curve, ...)` (`aease` exact).  `bounce_hits(2.bars, count:, elasticity:, decay:)` makes bouncing-ball rhythms.  Demos `bin/songs/tween_song.rb`, `bin/songs/bouncing_ball.rb`.

### [Tempo sync](tempo_sync.md)

`Sequence::Duration` lengths (`3.n16`, `2.bars`) work wherever lengths do; `1.beat.hz` is a Pitch from a `Sequence::TempoNode` whose tones lock their phase to the timeline, and `sig.delay(1.n8.dotted)` follows the tempo.  `Session` finds `TimelineNode`s in every graph.  The Transport's tempo is a `Sequence::TempoMap` of steps, ramps, and followed sources (`bpm 140, over: 4.bars`, `accel`/`rit`, `bpm :tempo`), journaled and undoable, rendered in 800-run-frame cells so it is the same at any buffer size; meters are a map too (`meter 7, 8`).  Build-time conversions read `Sequence.current_transport`.

### [Multichannel](multichannel.md)

Every node has `outputs`/`channel_count`; `GraphNode::Channels` is the bundle (`stereo(l, r)`, `channels(a, b, c)`; Array-like but deliberately not Enumerable: `.to_a` for `shuffle` etc.).  DSL calls on bundles run per channel with NumPy-style broadcasting (per-channel arguments via bundles or `per_channel(list | a..b)`; `per_voice` in synth voices); `reverb` is the exception (one reverb for all channels).  Conversions are `GraphNode::ChannelMixer` nodes (`pan`/`balance`, `width`, `mono`, `swap`, `mid_side`, `matrix`, `place`, `left`/`right`); sample all outputs of a mixer in turn.

## Sound

### [Oscillators and antialiasing](oscillators.md)

`Tone` waveforms are antialiased by default (`lib/mb/sound/band_limit.rb`, `fast_synth`: PolyBLEP/PolyBLAMP saws, squares, triangles, minBLEP sync, closed-form `complex_*` trains), each with a naive `a*` twin (`asaw`, ...) for lo-fi and control signals; plain sines are naive, `.lfo` fades band-limiting in.  Wavetables (`lib/mb/sound/wavetable.rb`, `fast_wavetable`), unison and swarms (`lib/mb/sound/unison.rb`), FM feedback, PWM/skew, and deliberate aliasing (`decimate`) live here too.  Phases are in cycles; randomness comes from `MB::Sound.seed`; tones give the same samples at any block size; measure with `bin/aliasing.rb`.

### [Envelopes](envelopes.md)

`MB::Sound::Envelope` (`fast_envelope`, mirror `Envelope.process_ruby`) is a state machine over curved segments landing exactly on target at whole samples: curves in signed dB (presets `:analog` default, `:snappy`, `:pad`, ...), shapes `:exp`/`:s`, multi-segment `env([[level, time, curve, shape], ...], release_at:, loop:)`, inputs `gate:`/`trigger:`/`velocity:`/`choke:`, and `.sensitivity(range | nil)` / `.no_velocity` in chains.  Constructors `adsr`, `env`, `amp_env`, `fm_env`, `filter_env`, `sq80_env`.  Kernel "runs" specialize only on constants of the patch (user rule).

### [Filter System](filters.md)

`lib/mb/sound/filter/` has 16+ filter types (`#process`/`#reset`; `Filter::Cookbook` designs).  Graph cookbook filters (`node.filter(:lowpass, cutoff:, quality:)`, `peq`) build `Filter::SVF`, whose parameters may move every sample (`structure: :biquad` for the old biquad); `sig.lp4(cutoff, resonance:)` is a CEM3379-style 4-pole and `sig.diode(...)` a TB-303-style ladder with the same knobs (`v.reso(...)` in voices); `sig.formant(:a, :o, morph:, voice:, shift:, width:)` five vowel bandpasses.  Convention: where mb-sound departs from its hardware model the playable version is `:musical` (default) and the faithful one `:hardware`.  Filter states flush denormals on an 800-sample grid of their own time, so tails match at any buffer size.

### [Delays](delays.md)

`#delay` (`Filter::Delay`) and `#multitap` share `MB::Sound::DelayLine` (C reads, exact mirrors; `:sinc` interpolation by default, `:cubic`, `:linear`); times are any length or node (`96.samples`, `3.n16`, `lfo.samples`), `feedback:`/`wet:`/`dry:` numbers or nodes, and delays ring out after their input ends (`MB::Sound::RingOut`).  Delay networks (`FastDelay.network`) build `multitap(t1, t2, feedback: [g1, g2] | g)`, `ping_pong(t, feedback:, spread:, mix:, input: :mono | :stereo)`, and `haas(15.ms, side:)`; tape echoes are `sig.tape_echo(:reel | :slapback | :ping_pong | :dub, time:, feedback:, mix:, tone:, low_cut:, drive:, wow:, flutter:)` (library family `:delay`).  Same output at any buffer size.

### [Chorus](chorus.md)

`sig.chorus(:juno1 | :juno2 | :juno12 | :lush, rate:, depth:, mix:, bbd: false)` (`GraphNode::Chorus`, self-contained in `graph_node/chorus.rb` and `chorus_nodes.rb` for a later effects project) is a Juno-60-style two-tap chorus returning a stereo bundle: mono in like the Juno, clean by default, `bbd: true` adds the board's filters and hiss.

### [Reverbs](reverbs.md)

`#reverb` (`GraphNode::Reverb`, kernel `fast_reverb`, mirror `MB_SOUND_REVERB=ruby`) is the one reverb: `[l, r].reverb(:hall)` runs inputs through diffusion, a per-sample FDN, and output taps with energy-normalized gains.  Presets `:room`, `:hall`, `:stadium`, `:space`, `:plate`, `:shimmer`, `:gated`, `:drone`, ...; the friendly form takes `room_size:`, `decay:`, `damping:`, `mix:`; options for modulation, in-loop filters, drive, crush, shimmer, freeze, and stretch, plus `duck:` and `gate:` after the network.  Unlike other DSL calls on bundles, one reverb serves all channels.

### [Dynamics (compressor, compander, ducking, limiter, multiband)](dynamics.md)

One compander core (`GraphNode::Dynamics`, `fast_dynamics`, exact mirrors): a dB peak/RMS detector (linked, any `sidechain:`), a transfer curve, a log-domain smoother, `lookahead:`, `makeup:`, `mix:`; same output at any buffer size.  Faces `compress`, `expand`, `noise_gate`, `duck(kick)`, `compand(...)`, `limit(ceiling: -1.db, lookahead: 1.5.ms, release:, true_peak: true)`, `bands(200.hz, 2000) { |lo, mid, hi| [...] }` crossovers, `mono_below`, and `squeeze`; trigger tracks (`sidechain :pump, clip`) key ducks with a line nobody hears.  Levels and gains are written `-12.db` (exact dB); bare numbers are linear gains and bare negatives raise.

### [Drum machines](drums.md)

`tr808(source, **knobs)` and `tr909(source, **knobs)` (`lib/mb/sound/drums.rb`, `drums/`) are `Drums::Kit`s of resonator, metal-bank, noise, and sample voices, played by a grid `Sequence::Kit` or any MIDI source, with per-voice knob Hashes, accents, chokes, flams, and `outputs: :separate`.  The kit builder (`kit { voice :kick do |h| ... end; choke ... }`, `Drums::Machine`/`Builder`/`Hit`) makes custom kits that tracks, recording, and swaps treat like an 808.  Idle voices sleep only on the 800-sample `Synth::SKIP_GRID` and wake on the exact hit, so output is the same at any buffer size.

### [Sampler](sampler.md)

`MB::Sound::Sample` (`lib/mb/sound/sample.rb`, `sample/`) is an immutable sound in memory (files, arrays, `bounce` of a graph, `capture_audio` live) with a root note, loop points, and cheap views (slices, reverse, loops, fades); edits (`bits`, `lofi`, `stretch`, `mono`) make new audio.  `Sample::Slices` name and chop breaks into clips with pitch marks; `Sampler::Instrument` maps regions to keys, velocities, and round robins, also from SFZ (`sfz`) and SoundFont 2 (`sf2`, pure Ruby).  `GraphNode::SamplerVoice` + `fast_sampler` (exact mirror `Sampler::KernelRuby`) plays them from the exact note-on sample, band-limited, with a 64-sample declick; a plan boundary.  Help `help :sampler`, `lesson :chop`.

### [Textures: dust, drift, modal resonators](textures.md)

Texture nodes in `fast_texture` and `fast_resonator` (exact Ruby mirrors, the same at any buffer size): `dust` sparse random impulses, `drift` random points joined smoothly (B-spline, holds, jitter, any Curve), `trig.resonate(:bowl | :gong | :bell | ...)` modal banks with physically motivated ratios and beating doublets (`GraphNode::ModalResonator`), `noise(:pink)`/`noise(:brown)`, and `sig.sounding(hold:, fade:)`, a gate open while a sound is above -90 dB.  Randomness is splitmix64, seeded per node.  Help `help :textures`, `help :recipes`; demo `bin/songs/critters.rb`.

### [Granular synthesis and spectral time-stretching](granular.md)

`sample.grains(density:, size:, position:, scan:, pitch:, ...)` (aliases `granular`, `cloud`; `GraphNode::Grains`, a stereo MultiOutput and a plan boundary) plays a cloud of windowed reads of a Sample's band-limited levels, every option a number, Length, knob, or node read per grain onset; `v.grains(sample, ...)` key-tracks in synth voices.  Kernel `FastSampler.grains` (exact mirror `Granular::KernelRuby`): onsets on exact samples, six splitmix64 draws per onset, a fixed number of slots.  `Sample#stretch(r, mode:)` offers `:cyclic` (S950), `:spectral` (phase vocoder with identity phase locking and kept transients), `:paul` (Paulstretch), and `:slice` (loops.md), with `randomize:` between vocoder and Paulstretch phases.  Help `help :granular`.

### [Loop files, slice stretch, tempo-following loops](loops.md)

`Sample['loop.wav']` reads loop metadata without ffmpeg's help (`Sample::Riff`: ACID tempo/beats/meter/root, `smpl` loops, cue labels as `sample.markers`), then FLAC tags, then tempo and key words in file and folder names (`Sample::LoopInfo`, reasons in `meta[:why]`), or detects the tempo (`detect: true`).  `stretch(r, mode: :slice)` (`Sample::SliceStretch`) moves slices to scaled times with exact attacks; `sample.follow` (`GraphNode::LoopPlayer`, a TimelineNode and plan boundary) plays a loop in time with the session tempo (slice stretch for percussive loops, spectral for tonal ones).  Console `loops(dir, bpm:, key:, beats:)` lists a folder from headers and names only.  Help `help :loops`.

### [SQ-80 voice, patches, and (designed) SysEx import](sq80.md)

`sq80(source = nil, :patch, **settings)` (`SQ80Methods`, `lib/mb/sound/sq80/`) is the SQ-80-flavored voice as a library patch: original tables only (nothing from the ROM), three oscillators into a driven lp4, panel-unit `sq80_env` envelopes; settings merge over `SQ80::Voice::DEFAULTS`, patches in `SQ80::PATCHES` (presets `preset :sq80_glass, midi:`), printed as `sq80(clip, :chop, ...)`.  The wave voices (`wave_voice(midi, :digibrass | :organ_reso | :square_bass, grit:)`) ship as presets.  SysEx programs parse (`SQ80::SysEx`, `SQ80::Program`); mapping them onto the voice is designed only.  Never commit real .syx banks or anything derived from them; SQ-80 is banned from demos for now.

## Notes and structure

### [Sequences](sequences.md)

`lib/mb/sound/sequence/`: immutable `Clip`s of `Event`s in exact Rational whole notes, built with `seq(C4, E4, G4.n4).n8`, chord steps, `grid('x...x...')`, and note length methods; a clip is a MIDI source (`clip.stream`, `clip.notes`, `clip.synth(voices:) { |v, i| }`) whose edges land on exact samples at the shared `Transport`'s tempo.  Transforms (legato, transpose, ratchet, swing, humanize, chance, groove, ghost chords, ...) share their cores with the MIDI stream transforms (`Sequence::Feel`) and run per row on grid Kits (`rotate` wraps, `shift` drops); `clip.show` draws them as text; clips carry controller lanes and note marks (accent `!A1`, slide `~A1`, flam), remember what plays them (`Sequence::PlayedBy`), and `swap` changes a player's clips on the next bar.  `!` is overridden only on Note and Step: test with `nil?`, never `!x`.

### [Generative music](generative.md)

A generator is a looping Clip whose events per cycle are a pure function of (seed, cycle): every draw is counter-based (`Generative::Dice`, splitmix64 over the seed and a key path, C `fast_generative` with an exact Ruby mirror), so cycles come out the same cold or in order (seeks, takes, documents, any buffer size).  Probability scales (`Weights`, `Chord`, `Field`, `Harmony`) are printable values with operators; `generate`, `strikes`, `melody`, `motifs` (phrase memory), and `beats` (evolving drum rows) make generator clips, steerable by knobs read once per cycle at a decision point; `markov` and `lsystem` write long forms that `flow { generate ... }` plays and `Form::Plan` works out ahead.  Help `help :generative`, `help :long_form`.

### [MIDI](midi.md)

`lib/mb/sound/midi/` is pull-based (no callbacks; only live input reads a clock): Sources (`FileSource`, `ClipSource`, `LiveSource`) make `MIDI::Event`s, `MIDI::Stream`s share them among readers and make transform views (`echo`, `arp`, `chord`, `humanize`, `quantize`, `lock`, ...), `MB::Sound::Notes` (`v` in synth code) turns them into signal nodes, and `Synth` allocates voices through `MIDI::Allocator` lanes.
Moving parameters (`MIDI::Param`: `cc(...)`, knobs, tempo LFOs, clips) are read once per decision; the session key and `MIDI::Lock` styles map keys into scales; `midi_clip`/`midi_kit` import MIDI files as clips in exact whole notes.
Live MIDI uses JACK ports when a server answers, else bundled RtMidi; specs use synthetic MIDI files only (the maintainer's `tmp/music/` is private).

### [Structure analysis (music information retrieval)](structure.md)

`analyze_form(source)` (alias `analyze_structure`; `StructureMethods`, `lib/mb/sound/structure.rb` + `structure/`, pure Ruby + Numo, ~120x realtime) finds tempo, beats, bars, and meters in a file, audio data, or a graph and returns a `Structure::Result` (`transport`, `meters_ruby`).  Our own renders use the render's exact grid; imported audio is tracked (comb-autocorrelation tempo, a constant-tempo beat grid, a downbeat Viterbi allowing 2- and 3-beat bars).  Phase S1 is built; sections, letter labels, and `:analysis` markers are S2.

## Session and set

### [Arrangement and the Session groundwork](arrangement.md)

The Session groundwork: `Session::Stamp` (frame + Rational position), `Session::Journal`, and one change queue (`Session#change`) through which every command lands on an exact sample, with mute/solo, undo, launch points (`on:`/`in:`/`at:`), and takes that replay exactly at any buffer size.
On top, the Set layer (`MB::Sound::Arrangement`, `Session#arrangement`): `track`, `scene`, `go`, the clip matrix (`launch`, `tweak`), ring-outs, song forms (`flow` with labels, gotos, picks, fills), seeks, markers, knobs (`knob`, `turn`, scenes and sections turning them), clocks, and recording (`arm`, `rec`, `capture`, `rec_audio`).
Rules: changes go through `Session#change`; scene graphs build on the scheduler thread ahead of their landing and new graphs are warmed in a sandbox first; never enable a TracePoint in library code (YJIT drops its compiled code); Sessions keep one instance variable layout.

### [Master effects](master_effects.md)

`Session#master` / console `master { |mix| mix.softclip }` runs the mix through a chain of `GraphNode::MixSource` channels; new chains start at launch points with the old one spilling over (`fade:` crossfades), `master nil` bypasses, and the master gain applies before the chain (`post: true` after it).
Without a chain, realtime live output ends in a transparent -1 dBFS `Session::SafetyLimiter` (never in renders, stems, takes, taps).
Mastering presets (`master :club`, `:streaming`, `:quiet`, `:vinyl`; `mix.master(:club)` anywhere; `masters`) are frozen `Mastering::Preset` values: renders reach their loudness target exactly in two passes (`Mastering::Targeting`), live uses the preset's drive or `ride: true`.

### [Buses, sends, and bus sidechains](buses.md)

`bus(:verb) { |sig| sig.reverb(:hall, mix: 1) }` (`Session::Buses`, console `BusMethods`: `bus`, `buses`, `feed`, `routes`) makes a named bus, a master-like chain (`Master::Chain` machinery) with its own input, into the master or another bus (`to:`; loops refused).
Routing belongs to player names: `track(:keys, send: { verb: -12.db })`, `track(:kick, to: :drums)`, `bg ..., send:`; sends are post-fader, and `feed :keys, :verb, -6.db, over: 2` is a journaled, undoable `:send` change.
Readers (`GraphNode::BusTap`: `duck(:drums)`, `duck(:drums, only: :kick)`, `bus(:drums)`) work anywhere; buses ring out and sleep on the 800-frame grid, so output is the same at any buffer size; `render(stems:)` stems sum to the pre-master mix.

### [CUE and MAIN: auditioning before launch](cue.md)

`cue :acid, sound` (console `CueMethods`, `Session::Cue`, `Arrangement::Cue`) plays a part on CUE (headphones) only, as player `:"acid/cue"`, in time with the set; `launch :acid` renames that same Player to `:acid` on its exact landing frame, ramping MAIN in and CUE out over `fade:`; `cue :drums` pre-listens a playing part (PFL), `cue :drop` cues a scene's changed tracks; `uncue`, `cues`.
CUE is dry (pre-bus, pre-master) and never reaches renders, stems, or taps; phones blend with knobs `:phones`/`:cue_mix`, and `cue_output` puts CUE on channels 3-4, split left/right, or off.

### [Racks, typed ports, and the inspection protocol](racks.md)

A `MB::Sound::Rack` (`lib/mb/sound/rack.rb`, console `RackMethods`) is a frozen, Proc-like reusable graph with typed ports (`:notes`, `:audio`, `:control`): `mrack`, `irack`, `arack`, `lrack`/`amrack`, `modrack`, `rack(name, in:, out:, **ports)`; apply with `src.then(&r)`, `r.(src)`, `stream.through(r)`, each application building a fresh subgraph on the bound values, so no node sits at a port.
Named racks join `Session::Names`; `knob :space, 0.3` inside a rack block makes a rack knob (`Rack::KnobInfo`, `:"dub/space"`, per player once two instances play).
Rack documents (`save :dub, rack(:dub)`, format 4) and graph documents carrying rack definitions reload bit for bit; every Traversable answers `port_info`, `params`, and frozen `param_info`/`param_snapshot` for UI threads.

### [Genre templates (`lib/mb/sound/genre.rb`, `genre/`, console `GenreMethods`)](genres.md)

`genre :dnb` (`GenreMethods`, `lib/mb/sound/genre.rb` + `genre/`) is a frozen `Genre::Template` of what the persona panel learned about a genre: tempo and range, meter, phrases, key, a `Form`, drum `Kit`s with fills, material clips, roles (patches with levels, params, filters, ducks, bus routes), scenes, knobs, `Mix` targets, and tips, for `:dnb`, `:jungle`, `:ambient`, `:funk`, `:house`, `:techno`.  Templates compose (`genre(:dnb, tempo: 170)`, a builder block, `like`, `Genre.define`), set up and play a Session (`t.setup`, `t.play`, `t.short(60)`), print back (`t.to_ruby`), and grow generated forms (`t.generative(seed:)`, `t.endless`).  Demo `bin/songs/genre_demo.rb -G dnb`; help `help :genres`.

## Console, UI, and scripts

### [Method Modules](method_modules.md)

`MB::Sound` extends topic modules that make the console API of `bin/sound.rb`: `IOMethods`, `PlaybackMethods` (`play`, `bg`, the background `Session`, `render`), `ScheduleMethods`, `ArrangementMethods`, `TransportMethods`, `PlotMethods`, `AnalysisMethods`, and about 20 more (Generation, Envelope, Midi, Sequence, Knob, Rack, ...).  `play`/`bg`/`render`/`write` share one conversion, `MB::Sound::Playable.graph`, which turns graphs, files, samples, clips, instruments, wavetables, and presets into a graph or a friendly `Playable::Unplayable`.  Plumbing that isn't a console command goes in `MB::Sound::Internal` (not extended, so it stays out of tab completion).

### [Console help](help.md)

Console help (`lib/mb/sound/help.rb` + `help/`, loaded by bin/sound.rb or on first use): `help` (the one-screen sheet), `help :knobs` (topics), `help :turn` (method pages from doc comments), `help /reson/` (search), `help node`, `now`, `demo`, and `lesson :set` (runnable lessons); every page is built with `Help::Doc` and shown through `Help.show`.  `help.level` sets the listening level as the live-only monitor trim.  The guard spec `spec/lib/mb/sound/help_spec.rb` requires every public console command to be in a topic (`help/content/topics.rb`), on the sheet, or exempt with a reason, and every example to play near the level tone.

### [The mb-sound tutorial (design for a later phase)](help_tutorial.md)

A design, not yet built, for a full vimtutor-style tutorial in the live console: a `tutorial` command whose chapters are lessons on the existing `Help.lesson` framework (help.md), one small A-minor piece grown from a single tone to a form with knobs and a recording, and checks that listen (`playing?`, `level_of`, knob values, landed changes) after every line typed.  Part 1 (sound basics) is about 30 minutes, the whole 2-3 hours.

### [Plotting](plotting.md)

`MB::Sound::Plot` (`lib/mb/sound/plot/`) draws every plot in pure Ruby (no gnuplot; `spec/support/no_gnuplot.rb` fails specs that start it): Scales -> Coords -> Marks -> guides -> Chart/Figure -> renderers for terminal text (looks `Plot::Text::LOOKS`, Braille `:scope` by default), SVG, PNG, and inline images.  Build with `Plot.chart { x :time; line data }`, `Plot.figure { chart { ... } }`, the presets (`Plot.waveform`, `spectrum`, ...), or the console's `chart`/`figure`/`plot`; charts `show`, `to_svg`, and `save('x.svg' | .png | .txt | .ans | .html)`.  Live panes use `Plot::Live` over the C text kernels in `fast_ui` (exact mirrors of the Ruby; `MB_SOUND_PLOT=ruby`), and UI panes never write their own bytes.

### [Terminal UI](terminal_ui.md)

`ui` (`lib/mb/sound/ui.rb` + `ui/`) is the live terminal UI: a read-only dashboard band under the console (`ui :deck`, `ui :mini`), or `ui :tiles`/`:studio`, which own the alternate screen and tile panes around the real Pry on an in-process pty (the generic layers are the mb-term gem, `gems/mb-term/`, `MB::Term`).  The render thread publishes one frozen `UI::Snapshot` per buffer the painter takes; `UI::Poll` reads slow data 4/s; a painter thread draws panes (Ruby: `pane`, `layout`) into a C cell grid and writes changed cells in one synchronized frame.  Never poll `Session#players`/`#clock`/`#strip_info` from the painter (render lock), and panes never write their own bytes.

### [Sound-design screen (`ui :sound`)](sound_design_ui.md)

`ui :sound` (or `design :bass`) is the tiled screen for designing a track's sound: the patch inspector (`Panes::Inspector`: the voice in SOURCE FILTER AMP MOD FX sections, knobs turned with arrows, Enter types a value), the node's preview (`Plot::Panels`), the graph's code, and the RENDER pane (`UI::PatchRender`: a second copy of one voice, reset to its post-build snapshot and played one note in windows after the live render thread's buffers, showing a settled cycle, spectrum, and envelope).  A new track starts from the init voice (`preset :init`, `bin/synths/init_voice.rb`); live literals (`bind`) and build knobs rebuild a track's patch at its launch point.

### [Scripts](scripts.md)

Every bin/ script except the console `bin/sound.rb` uses a `ScriptingMethods` helper backed by `ScriptRunner`: `effect_script { |input, p| }`, `synth_script { |midi, p| }`, `song_script(bars:) { |p| }`, or `script(args:) { |args, p| }`, sharing `-o`, `-f`, `-g`, `-P`, `-q`, `-L`, `--ui [LAYOUT]`.
Parameters are options only (`name: [default, 'description', '-x', Type, range]`); graph-building code goes inside the block, loadable scripts are guarded with `if main_script?(__FILE__)`, and every script starts with the `RUBY_THREAD_TIMESLICE=10 MB_SOUND_YJIT=1` shebang (`spec/bin/shebang_spec.rb`), never `RUBY_YJIT_ENABLE=1`/`--yjit`.

## Audio I/O

### [Audio I/O](audio_io.md)

Device I/O goes through bundled miniaudio (`fast_audio`) plus a small JACK backend (one client per process, ports added any time); `OUTPUT_TYPE`/`INPUT_TYPE` pick `device`, `ffmpeg`, or `null`.
`DeviceOutput` writes a lock-free ring drained on the device thread (Ruby never on the audio thread), with latency profiles (`AUDIO_PROFILE`, `-L`, `latency :low`), resampling to the card's rate, and underrun concealment (`:repeat` by default).
Rules: never `jack_port_unregister` on an active JACK client; things closed at exit register with `ExitClose`, never their own `at_exit` block; bin/ scripts set `RUBY_THREAD_TIMESLICE=10` in their shebang.

### [Latency probe (`fast_latency`, `MB::Sound::LatencyProbe`, `bin/latency_probe.rb`)](latency_probe.md)

`bin/latency_probe.rb -t 1h` / `MB::Sound::LatencyProbe.start(dir:)` tells system stalls from mb-sound's own: `FastLatency::Probe` is a pthread outside the GVL on an absolute-deadline 1 ms loop timing a memory walk and a CPU loop, with per-second aggregates, histograms, and stall episodes in C, drained through a lock-free ring by a Ruby consumer; a Ruby ticker sees GVL/GC/YJIT stalls too, and `#watch(session)` logs slow buffers and underruns.
Reports give percentiles, top stalls with wall times, periodicity (":59.9 of each minute"), Ruby stalls by cause, and plots; `MB_SOUND_LATENCY_PROBE=1` probes any live script.
